title: Unit 13
subtitle: A tactical assignment built for a short return visit

body: Unit 13 is Zipper Interactive's PlayStation Vita third-person shooter, first released in North America on 6 March 2012. Its military operations are organised as individual missions with objectives and conditions that can change the approach required. Some allow several ways to complete the task, while others impose restrictions such as remaining unseen. The player uses the Vita's paired sticks to move and aim, bringing a familiar console-shooter arrangement to a handheld. A mission becomes a compact problem that can be attempted again with a clearer plan rather than only a chapter passed once.

Objectives can be completed in different orders, allowing the player to judge which route makes the operation more manageable. Dynamic mode changes objective and enemy locations, equipment and other conditions, giving a familiar environment another arrangement. Knowledge of the space remains useful without making every threat predictable. All missions can also be played cooperatively, turning the choice of route into something shared with another person. The structure encourages repeated visits because a location is treated as a set of tactical possibilities rather than a single fixed sequence of enemies and instructions.

Justin Burnett composed the music for a project released near the Vita's international launch. European and Japanese editions followed within days of North America. Unit 13 became the final game from Zipper Interactive before Sony closed the studio, ending a history closely associated with SOCOM and tactical console shooting. Its design carries that experience into a different format. Rather than depending entirely on a long cinematic campaign, it gives the handheld a collection of operations whose objectives, conditions and cooperative options can make a short session feel complete while still leaving another variation to attempt.
